reading.body:
Google does not publish megawatt capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for individual buildings at its Council Bluffs campus in Pottawattamie County, Iowa. The operator discloses only aggregate investment figures at the state level, making the specific scale of this site opaque to public analysis. This facility is one of 52 mapped data center sites in Iowa, but only two sites in the state have published power specifications, and those two totaling 18 MW rank this campus third by disclosed capacity despite having no disclosed figure of its own.

The Council Bluffs campus has operated since 2007 and is the anchor of Google's over $20 billion Iowa investment. A $7 billion expansion was announced for the campus, alongside a new Cedar Rapids site, paired with a NextEra Energy agreement to restart the Duane Arnold nuclear plant as part of regional power strategy. This signals sustained capital commitment and active pursuit of new generation capacity, but the timing and phasing of the expansion, and the power allocation between sites, are not published.

Without disclosed megawatt figures, the relevance of this campus to AI scaling cannot be read from specifications. The nuclear plant restart agreement suggests Google views the regional grid as a binding constraint on its growth, but whether the expansion targets this site or splits across Iowa, and how much new capacity it will actually command, remain undisclosed. For a reader evaluating grid constraints on AI, this campus represents material investment and clear strategic intent without transparent scale.
